questions.question: Identify the type of sentence used in the following line from the passage: "Deeply moved by the suffering he had caused, Ashoka underwent a profound transformation."
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the type of sentence used in the following line from the passage:

"Deeply moved by the suffering he had caused, Ashoka underwent a profound transformation."
questions.solution:
Among the given options, (a) Complex sentence is the correct answer because the line "Deeply moved by the suffering he had caused, Ashoka underwent a profound transformation" contains one independent clause ("Ashoka underwent a profound transformation") and one dependent clause introduced by the participial phrase "Deeply moved by the suffering he had caused," which functions adjectivally. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The other options are incorrect as (b) compound sentences have two independent clauses, (c) simple sentences have only one independent clause without subordination, and (d) compound-complex sentences have at least two independent and one dependent clause.

Note:

A participial phrase consists of a participle (a verb form used as an adjective) along with its modifiers, objects, and complements. The participle can be in the present form (ending in -ing) or the past form (usually ending in -ed, -en, or other irregular forms). For example:

Present participle: "Running quickly through the field, he passed everyone." (Here, "Running quickly through the field" describes "he.").

Past participle: "The vase, broken by the cat, lay on the floor." (In this case, "broken by the cat" describes "the vase.").

The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['been'] and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Perfect. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Perfect.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + had + been + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + had + V3 + Object.

For example:

She had been called by me. (Passive Voice)

I had called her. (Active Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): The residents had filed a formal complaint against the company before the investigation was officially launched.

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

questions.question: Identify the sentence from the passage which is in the passive voice:
questions.questionHtml: Identify the sentence from the passage which is in the passive voice:

options.text: These fragments represent a complex and growing threat, contaminating ecosystems from the deepest ocean trenches to the very air we breathe.
options.html: These fragments represent a complex and growing threat, contaminating ecosystems from the deepest ocean trenches to the very air we breathe.

options.text: Marine life, from microscopic plankton to giant whales, often mistakes these plastic fragments for food.
options.html: Marine life, from microscopic plankton to giant whales, often mistakes these plastic fragments for food.

options.text: The sources of microplastic pollution are broadly divided into two categories: primary and secondary.
options.html: The sources of microplastic pollution are broadly divided into two categories: primary and secondary.

options.text: Scientists have now confirmed the presence of microplastics deep within the human body.
options.html: Scientists have now confirmed the presence of microplastics deep within the human body.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option c).

A sentence is in the passive voice when the subject of the sentence is the recipient of the action, not the performer of the action. The typical structure is subject + form of "to be" + past participle (v3).

In sentence (c), the subject is "The sources of microplastic pollution." The verb phrase is "are... divided." The sources are not doing the dividing; they are being divided by someone else (e.g., by scientists, by researchers). Since the subject is receiving the action, the sentence is in the passive voice.

Option a): The subject, "These fragments," is performing the action ("represent").

Option b): The subject, "Marine life," is performing the action ("mistakes").

Option d): The subject, "Scientists," is performing the action ("have confirmed").

Note:

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here, "Rita and her friends" (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here, 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the woman fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question: The figure of speech used in "A bicycle can't stand on its own because it is two-tired"?

questions.solution:
A pun is a form of wordplay that exploits the different possible meanings of a word or the fact that there are words that sound alike but have different meanings (homophones).

The given joke hinges entirely on the possible dual meaning of the phrase "two-tired":

Literal Meaning: A bicycle has two tires.

Sound-Alike Meaning: The phrase sounds exactly like "too tired," meaning overly fatigued.

The humour comes from this clever play on words.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Option a): Giving human qualities or actions to inanimate objects. The sentence does give a human-like quality (being "tired") to a bicycle. However, the primary purpose of the sentence is not to make the bicycle seem human, but to make a joke based on wordplay. The personification is a result of the pun, not the main device itself.

Option b): A figure of speech where two contradictory terms are placed together. Example: "Deafening silence" or "jumbo shrimp."

Option d): A comparison between two different things using "like" or "as." Example: "The joke was as old as the hills."

questions.question: Which among the following sentences uses the article (if required) before the word 'Atlantic' correctly?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following sentences uses the article (if required) before the word 'Atlantic' correctly?

options.text: The ship is crossing Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.
options.html: The ship is crossing Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.

options.text: The ship is crossing an Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.
options.html: The ship is crossing an Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.

options.text: The ship is crossing a Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.
options.html: The ship is crossing a Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.

options.text: The ship is crossing the Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.
options.html: The ship is crossing the Atlantic Ocean to reach New York.

questions.solution:
The governing rule in this case is that the definite article "the" must be used before the names of specific, unique geographical features, including oceans, seas, rivers, canals, deserts, and mountain ranges.

Option a): Incorrect. This sentence omits the required article. "Atlantic Ocean" is a proper noun referring to a specific, unique body of water. According to English grammar rules for geographical names of this type, the definite article "the" must precede it. The omission of the article makes the sentence grammatically incomplete.

Option b): Incorrect. This sentence uses the indefinite article "an". Indefinite articles ("a" or "an") are used for non-specific, singular nouns. The Atlantic Ocean is a single, unique, and specific entity; there is only one. Using "an" incorrectly implies that it is one of many "Atlantic Oceans," which is not meaningful.

Option c): Incorrect. This sentence also uses an incorrect indefinite article. The reasoning is the same as for option (b): the indefinite article "a" is inappropriate for a unique proper noun. Furthermore, "a" is used before words starting with a consonant sound. "Atlantic" begins with a vowel sound, so even if an indefinite article were permissible, "an" would be the phonetically correct choice, not "a". This option is incorrect on two grammatical points.

Option d): Correct. This sentence correctly uses the definite article "the". As "Atlantic Ocean" is the name of a unique geographical feature, the definite article is required to specify it. This is the standard and grammatically correct construction.

Comparative examples: the Pacific Ocean, the Nile River, the Sahara Desert, the Alps.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.question: Select the sentence with the correct use of article 'the.'
questions.questionHtml: Select the sentence with the correct use of article 'the.'

options.text: The Mount Everest is the highest peak in the entire world.
options.html: The Mount Everest is the highest peak in the entire world.

options.text: They went on a cruise that sailed across the Mediterranean Sea.
options.html: They went on a cruise that sailed across the Mediterranean Sea.

options.text: We visited the beautiful Lake Como during our trip to Italy.
options.html: We visited the beautiful Lake Como during our trip to Italy.

options.text: I would love to hike in the Rocky Mountain National Park one day.
options.html: I would love to hike in the Rocky Mountain National Park one day.

questions.solution:
The use of the definite article "the" with geographical names follows specific rules.

Use "the" with: Oceans, seas, rivers, canals (e.g., the Pacific Ocean, the Mediterranean Sea, the Nile River); Mountain ranges (e.g., the Alps, the Rocky Mountains); Deserts (e.g., the Sahara); Groups of islands (e.g., the Bahamas).

Do NOT use "the" with: Single mountains or peaks (e.g., Mount Everest, Mount Fuji); Individual lakes (e.g., Lake Como, Lake Superior); Continents, most countries, states, and cities (e.g., Europe, Japan, California, Paris); Most parks with proper names (e.g., Yellowstone National Park, Central Park).

Option a): Incorrect. "Mount Everest" is the name of a single, individual mountain peak. According to the rule, single mountains do not take the definite article "the".

Correct version: "Mount Everest is the highest peak in the entire world."

Option b): Correct. "Mediterranean Sea" is the name of a sea. The rule requires the use of the definite article "the" before the names of seas, oceans, and rivers. This sentence correctly applies that rule.

Option c): Incorrect. "Lake Como" is the name of an individual lake. Individual lakes do not take the definite article. The presence of the adjective "beautiful" does not change this rule.

Correct version: "We visited beautiful Lake Como during our trip to Italy."

Option d): Incorrect. While the mountain range is called "the Rocky Mountains," the official proper name of the park is "Rocky Mountain National Park." Like other named parks (e.g., Yellowstone National Park), it does not take the definite article.

Correct version: "I would love to hike in Rocky Mountain National Park one day."

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note: Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles; they refer to, or introduce, an unspecified noun.

questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Unwanted expenses have incur this month.
questions.solution:
The verb 'have' in the underlined phrase is to be followed by a verb in the past participle form (V3) but the verb 'incur' is in the base form. Also, a 'to-be' form of verb is required as the sentence is in Passive voice. Among the options, 'have been incurred' in option (d) is the best replacement for the underlined phrase both contextually and grammatically. 'Has been incurred' may lead to subject-verb agreement error (singular verb "has" cannot be used for plural noun "expenses"), if used as the replacement and 'have incurred' is incorrect form of verb for a Passive voice sentence. So, these two options cannot be used and thus negated.

The correct sentence is: Unwanted expenses have been incurred this month.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - She likes cooking. [singular subject and verb] -- They like to cook vegetables. [plural subject and verb]

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Perfect Tense or Past Simple Tense.

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

OR

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

The passage explicitly states that the cause of the Flynn Effect "is not attributed to a single factor but is likely the result of a combination of environmental and societal advancements." [second paragraph]

The second and third paragraphs then elaborate on these factors:

Environmental: "improved nutrition and healthcare," "healthier brain development," and "environmental complexity" (exposure to technology, complex work).

Educational: "expansion and evolution of formal education," which trains people in abstract thought and logical reasoning.

Option a): The passage directly refutes this by stating, "The Flynn Effect does not necessarily mean humans have become innately more intelligent..." [last paragraph] Innate intelligence refers to inborn, or genetic, intelligence.

Option c): The passage treats the Flynn Effect as a real, documented phenomenon and explores its causes. It never suggests that the effect is an illusion caused by faulty tests.

Explanation of Statements:

Statement 1 is True. Mitochondria contain their own small, circular chromosome (mtDNA), separate from the nuclear DNA of the cell. They also have their own ribosomes and can replicate through a process similar to binary fission. However, they are only "semi-autonomous" because they rely on proteins encoded by the cell's nuclear DNA to function and replicate.

Statement 2 is True. The endosymbiotic theory is the leading explanation for the origin of mitochondria. It posits that an ancestral host cell engulfed an aerobic bacterium. Instead of being digested, the bacterium established a symbiotic relationship, eventually evolving into the mitochondrion.

Statement 2 explains Statement 1. The reason mitochondria have bacteria-like features (circular DNA, semi-autonomous replication) is a direct consequence of their evolutionary origin from a free-living bacterium, as described by the endosymbiotic theory.

Further Insights:

Other evidence supporting the endosymbiotic theory includes the fact that mitochondria have a double membrane (the inner membrane corresponding to the original bacterial membrane and the outer one from the host cell's vesicle) and have ribosomes that are more similar to prokaryotic ribosomes than eukaryotic ones.

A similar process is believed to have led to the evolution of chloroplasts in plant cells from an engulfed cyanobacterium.

ii is Incorrect. The reactivity series of metals dictates which element can displace another. Since iron successfully displaces copper from the solution, it demonstrates that iron is more reactive than copper, not the other way around. The reddish-brown deposit is the less reactive copper metal precipitating out of the solution.

iii is Correct. The initial blue color of the solution is due to the presence of hydrated copper(II) ions (Cu⁺). As the reaction proceeds, these are replaced by iron(II) ions (Fe⁺) from the newly formed iron(II) sulfate (FeSO₄). Aqueous solutions containing Fe⁺ ions are typically pale green.

This experiment is a common way to demonstrate the relative positions of iron and copper in the reactivity series.

questions.question: What is the function of Gibberellins in plants? पौधों में जिबरेलिन का क्या कार्य है?
questions.solution: Gibberellins (GAs) are plant hormones that regulate growth and influence various developmental processes, including stem elongation, germination, dormancy, flowering, sex expression, enzyme induction, and leaf and fruit senescence. Gibberellins play an important role in several developmental stages in plants, but their claim to fame is making stems longer. Gibberellins promote stem elongation between nodes on the stem. A node is a place on a stem where a leaf attaches, so gibberellins elongate the internodes. It is easiest to see the absence of gibberellin in dwarf plants and rosette plants - there is very little space between nodes on a stem and the leaves are clustered toward the base of the plant.
